name: Humor Effect
description: Humorous material is often remembered better than equivalent nonhumorous material. The effect is about memorability, not a blanket claim that humorous interfaces are always better or more usable.
design_relevance_note: Most relevant to instructional content, onboarding, marketing surfaces, empty states, and microcopy where memorability matters; it does not justify injecting jokes into serious, high-stakes, or trust-sensitive flows by default.
prevalence_note: Sometimes invoked in education, onboarding, and brand-voice work, but not a standard general UX law and usually absent from core heuristic-evaluation canons.

findings.description: Sentence-memory experiments found humorous material can be remembered better than comparable nonhumorous material, directly backing the core claim behind the humor effect.
findings.source_title: Effects of humor on sentence memory.
findings.source_venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
